title: Priority-aware micro-batching + kernel probing to cut embedding p99
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Reduce end-to-end p95/p99 latency for the /embeddings endpoint under mixed workloads by combining priority-aware micro-batching with a lightweight kernel probing and soft-fallback mechanism. Background: recent production tails show a 3x p99 increase during bursty small requests that collide with large-sequence tasks and cold kernel choices. Current schedulers only consider arrival time and queue length; kernel selection is deterministic from the model profile and often picks a high-throughput path that suffers for small sequence lengths. Approach: 1) Implement request priority tagging (interactive vs batch) and a small-window scheduler that forms prioritized micro-batches with max-wait knobs per priority. 2) Add a kernel-probing step for the first few requests per newly-provisioned worker to capture per-GPU performance for short vs long sequences; persist a lightweight hint cache to avoid probing on every request. 3) Introduce a soft-fallback runtime that can switch to a low-latency kernel variant when micro-batch sizes are below a threshold or KV cache hit rates are low. 4) Evaluate trade-offs: potential throughput loss from smaller batches, increase in kernel-switch overhead, and accuracy regressions from different quantization kernels. Success metrics: 25-40% reduction in embedding p99 for interactive traffic, <5% degradation of aggregate throughput, no increase in error rate. Timeline: spike + bench (1 week), implement scheduler + priority plumbing (2 weeks), kernel-probe + hint cache (1 week), rollout to canary (1 week), monitor + refine (2 weeks).
acceptance_criteria: Observable 25%+ reduction in p99 for interactive embedding traffic on staging under mixed workload replay
No more than 5% drop in overall throughput on the tested instance types
Kernel probe stores hints in worker-local cache and persists to central hintstore on graceful shutdown
Automated canary pipeline with rollback on p99 regression >10%
Design doc and parameter knobs documented in runtime-ops playbook
